tei:titleStmt.tei:title: Barchu: Bless Adonoy Who is blessed.

tei:availability.tei:p: Published by Sefaria under CC-BY, which Sefaria defines as Creative Commons Attribution 3.0.

tei:div.tei:head: It has become a universally-accepted custom to recite Barechu before proceeding to the blessings of Shema. Barechu, like Kaddish and Kedushah, cannot be recited unless a quorum—a minyan of ten adult males—is present. Barechu is also said by one who is called upon to read from the Torah. The practice of saying Barechu is mentioned numerous times in the Talmud. It is even cited in the Mishna (Maseches Berachos 49b) in the names of Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Yishmael.
tei:div.tei:p: The Chazzan says:Bless Adonoy Who is blessed.
